_notes: Assertions check Plugin API state after the run. No transcript-introspection (workflow expectations belong in SKILL.md and figma-worker.md, not here). Each assertion is a JS predicate against figma.* state. A runner should batch all predicates per eval into one IIFE returning {predicate: bool, ...} so the suite pays one agent-browser cold-start per eval, not one per predicate.

evals.prompt: Create a button component named Atoms/Button in my Figma file
evals.expected_output: A ComponentNode named Atoms/Button with Auto Layout and a Button text child
expectations: A ComponentNode with name === 'Atoms/Button' exists on the current page

evals.prompt: Change the heading text in my login screen to 'Welcome'
evals.expected_output: The heading text node updated to 'Welcome' with font preserved
expectations: The target TEXT node still exists (same id)

evals.prompt: Show me the structure of this Figma file
evals.expected_output: Page name, frame names, types, and IDs returned
expectations: Response includes current page name (non-empty string)
Response includes an array of top-level children with id, name, type for each
No mutations occurred: every child id in preState still exists post-run

evals.prompt: Build a card component with a title, description, and image placeholder
evals.expected_output: A component with Auto Layout containing title text, description text, and an image rectangle

evals.prompt: Add a drop shadow to the main frame in my Figma file
evals.expected_output: The frame has a DROP_SHADOW effect applied with existing effects preserved
expectations: every effect in preState.effects exists in node.effects (preserved, not replaced)

evals.prompt: Import https://example.com into my Figma file
evals.expected_output: A root frame named after the page title holding the page's text as TEXT nodes, with Auto Layout inferred from flow and a cumulative capture report
expectations: A FrameNode with name === '[cap:0] Example Domain' exists on the current page
every value in window.__batchState.captureIds resolves via figma.getNodeByIdAsync
